title: Shelve three returned books upright and brace the row with a bookend
instruction: Shelve the red, green and blue books from the tray upright on the shelf in one row, in any order, with no gaps, starting against the shelf's left end wall, then stand the black bookend against the right side of the last book.
context: Library shelvers stand returned books upright from the end of the shelf and brace every partial row with a bookend, because books left leaning or lying flat warp their spines and slump. Done by: library assistants and technicians, pages and shelvers, archive technicians.
setup: A fixed brown wooden shelf stands on the table: a 15 mm thick board 11 cm deep and 30 cm long, its front edge 22.5 cm and its back edge 33.5 cm in front of the arm bases, running right from 8 cm left of the midline to 22 cm right of it; a 1 cm thick end wall closes its left end and a 1 cm thick back wall stands along its back edge, both rising 8 cm above the board's top. A fixed dark grey plastic book return tray stands in front of the left arm, its centre 15 cm in front of the arm bases and 23 cm left of the midline: inside 9 cm front to back and 13 cm side to side, a 5 mm floor, 5 mm walls 4 cm tall, and two 5 mm dividers making three 40 mm wide slots. In the slots stand three pocket books (bound paper, 76 mm deep, 34 mm thick, 120 mm tall, 250 g each), upright with their 76 mm side pointing away from the arms: red in the left slot (27.5 cm left of the midline), green in the middle (23 cm), blue in the right (18.5 cm). A black acetal (POM) plastic bookend block (70 mm deep, 40 mm thick, 120 mm tall, 450 g) stands on the table in front of the right arm, its centre 15 cm in front of the arm bases and 22 cm right of the midline, its 70 mm side pointing away from the arms. Nothing else is on the table.
scoring: A book is shelved when, seen from above, no part of it is more than 1 cm beyond the board's edges, its bottom is within 2 mm of the board's top (set down, not held above it), its tall edges are at most 5 degrees from vertical, and its 76 mm side is within 10 degrees of front to back (either 76 mm end facing the arms). Gaps are measured side to side, seen from above, between the outermost points of the two objects (for a turned or leaning book, its corner or top edge). The row is built from the end wall: the shelved book nearest the wall is in it if at most 5 mm separates its leftmost point from the wall, the next one if at most 5 mm separates it from the previous book, and so on (touching or overlapping outlines count as 0 mm). Each book: 0.2 if in the row, or 0.1 if shelved but not in the row. The bookend, in any orientation: 0.4 if it stands on the board (no part more than 1 cm beyond the board's edges, bottom within 2 mm of its top, at most 5 degrees from vertical) against the right side of the third book of a complete row: its centre is right of the book's centre, its leftmost point is within 5 mm of the book's rightmost point (at most 5 mm right of it, or at most 5 mm left of it), and its left face overlaps the book's right face by at least 2 cm front to back; or 0.2 if it stands on the board otherwise while at least one book is in the row; 0 if no book is in the row. All three books in the row and the bookend against them: 1.0. The score is 0 if any book with its centre over the board is tilted more than 45 degrees (flat on its side or fore-edge), or any book rests on another book or the bookend (their outlines overlap seen from above and its bottom is within 1 cm of the other's top, above or below it); a book held more than 1 cm above the others doesn't count as resting on them.
reset_notes: Stand the three books back in the tray, red left, green middle, blue right, 76 mm sides pointing away from the arms; stand the bookend back at its mark in front of the right arm. The shelf and the tray are fixed (clamp or tape them down for real trials); tape outlines on the table make the reset quick.
fidelity: Approximate: each book is one rigid box, so covers and pages don't flex and a leaning book doesn't warp; the books are pocket-sized (76 mm deep) so the gripper can hold them by the front and back faces. The bookend is a plain block, not an L-shaped bookend. The shelf and tray are fixed in place. Every object has the same rubber-like friction (1.2 static, 1.0 dynamic), grippier than paper on wood.
